headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage: Dify’s broad egress and filesystem access can ingest caveman outputs and shared state without strong provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md, while Dify can use OpenAPI tools and shared server datastore. That creates a plausible bridge where caveman-generated content is fed into Dify workflows and treated as instructions. The pathway is not directly documented for this pair, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman output is copied into a Dify agent prompt or workflow input
IF Dify tools or workflows parse caveman-authored text as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all caveman outputs before handoff
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form caveman text into Dify prompts
Require a human review step before Dify executes any tool call based on caveman output
Use a fixed schema for caveman-to-Dify handoff fields
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Dify reads uploaded knowledge-base files and sends data to model providers and tool credentials. If the pair shares a workspace or file handoff, sensitive content can flow from caveman into Dify’s outbound API calls. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible but not explicitly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF caveman project notes or memory files are uploaded into Dify knowledge-base files
IF Dify workflows send those files or derived text to model providers or tools
mitigations: Keep caveman and Dify in separate directories
Do not upload caveman memory files or session logs into Dify
Redact secrets from project notes before any handoff
Restrict Dify tools to non-sensitive test data
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses files, while Dify supports multiple instances with shared state via its datastore and has write_filesystem plus broad network egress. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared artifacts, concurrent writes and state drift can corrupt outputs or overwrite each other. Because Dify’s write surface is explicit and caveman’s file surfaces are present, the conflict is credible and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory
IF Dify workflows persist artifacts that caveman also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Make one agent read-only on shared artifacts
Snapshot files before each agent run
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and Dify is an orchestration platform that can route agent outputs into tools or workflows. That makes it plausible for Dify to treat caveman text as authoritative and act on it without verification. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dify workflow steps consume caveman-generated text as facts or instructions
IF no validation step checks caveman outputs before tool execution
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations or source links for factual claims
Limit caveman output to drafts only
Have Dify mark caveman content as untrusted input
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and model-provider API keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into both systems, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific residency mismatch is documented here, so I rate this as medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman project notes or Dify conversation logs
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either system
Document retention settings for both tools
Delete stale logs and memory files after each task
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across systems
